suggestions.rationale: Clinical Mapping Master Resolution 2026 publishes this relationship only as phenotype specific temporal risk. Require documented cerebral malaria, rather than uncomplicated malaria, with subsequent separately diagnosed epilepsy after the acute cerebral-malaria episode. PMID 25631856 principally represents survivors of cerebral malaria, most of whom were children in malaria-endemic settings, and supports a population-level association with long-term neurologic sequelae. Do not infer epilepsy from uncomplicated malaria, malaria exposure alone, an acute febrile seizure, or an isolated seizure occurring only during the acute cerebral-malaria illness. The cited literature supports only this bounded proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-8 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Malaria can produce clinically significant anemia through hemolysis of infected and uninfected erythrocytes and impaired erythropoiesis; the relationship is strongest when anemia is temporally linked to active or recent malaria. Require established malaria and a separately documented anemia phenotype with compatible timing. Do not infer chronic anemia from remote resolved malaria. Preserve nutritional deficiency, blood loss, hemoglobinopathy, chronic kidney disease, marrow disease, hemolysis from other causes, and other competing etiologies. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
